question: Should OpenClaw treat `models.providers.*.request.headers.*` like top-level provider headers and suppress plaintext warnings when `isLikelySensitiveModelProviderHeaderName` says the header name is not credential-bearing?
rationale: The code change is mechanically small, but it deliberately changes when credential audit surfaces report plaintext request-header values, so automation cannot choose the security tradeoff on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Accept the shared request-header classifier
options.body: Record the policy, rebase the branch preserving current-main audit behavior, and merge the focused collector/test alignment.

options.title: Narrow the suppression
options.body: Keep request headers conservative by allowing only documented static routing headers or by expanding the sensitive-name classifier before merge.

options.title: Keep the current audit contract
options.body: Reject or pause the PR and leave all request-header plaintext strings warning until a safer audit contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Accept the shared request-header classifier
recommendation.body: Record the policy, rebase the branch preserving current-main audit behavior, and merge the focused collector/test alignment.

likelyOwner.reason: The request transport override and current request-header registry/classifier history make this the closest individual routing candidate, with secops/CODEOWNERS review still needed.
